title: xiom build
concept: `xiom build` compiles source code into an executable or library
why: Source code must be transformed into machine instructions before it runs. `xiom build` orchestrates this pipeline: parsing, type checking, optimization, code generation, and linking. Understanding the build command is essential — it's the bridge between your editor and a running program.
theory: `xiom build` processes the project defined by `package.xi` and all `.xi` files under `src/`. The compilation pipeline runs in stages: (1) lexing each file into tokens, (2) parsing into AST, (3) name resolution and type checking, (4) intermediate representation generation, (5) LLVM optimization, and (6) native code generation. Binary targets produce an executable in `target/`; library targets produce a `.xiomlib` file. Builds are incremental by default — only changed files are recompiled.
syntax_ref:
xiom build                    # debug build
xiom build --release          # optimized build
xiom build --target wasm      # cross-compile
code_template:
# Project structure:
# src/
#   main.xi
# package.xi

# Terminal:
# $ xiom build
#   Compiling my_app v0.1.0
#   Finished dev [unoptimized] in 0.8s
#   Binary: target/debug/my_app.exe

# $ target/debug/my_app.exe
# Hello, XIOM!
solution:
# Build and run workflow:
#
# 1. Create src/main.xi:
fn main() {
    io.println("Build successful!")
}
#
# 2. Build:
# $ xiom build
#   Compiling hello v0.1.0
#   Finished dev in 0.3s
#
# 3. Run the release build:
# $ xiom build --release
# $ target/release/hello
#   Build successful!
#
# 4. Check build artifacts:
# $ ls target/
#   debug/  release/
tips: Use `xiom build --release` for the final distributable binary
Watch for compiler warnings — they often catch real bugs
`xiom build --verbose` shows every compilation step in detail
common_mistakes: Forgetting to save files before building
Building from the wrong directory (must be project root)
Expecting `xiom build` to automatically fetch new dependencies
